anchors.raw: I think a number that I'll be more comfortable with is probably around $4,000 or $5,000. I'm not sure that's possible for Trevor to accommodate and so forth.
anchors.note: Anchored at two thirds to five sixths of the price, and framed as a comfort level rather than a ceiling. He restated it once as a direct request that Trevor be consulted at $5,000, and it was never answered — so the anchor is still live going into the 24 July call.

anchors.raw: I prefer not to. I just want to, you know, I can afford it. I'd rather just pay it. I just want to be comfortable as to when on the timing of it.
anchors.note: He declined third-party financing on principle while confirming capacity, and separately said 'In the grand scheme of things, not a lot of money, but it's a timing thing.' The wallet is open — the objection is a calendar objection wearing a price objection's clothes, and the rep treated it as the latter.

unmet_demand.want: To sign now but begin the programme and the payment cycle together around 1 August, once his large near-term commitments have cleared
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing in the offer supports a deferred start with a deferred payment cycle. Every lever the rep had — a shorter tier, an interest-free split, third-party financing — moves money earlier or reduces scope, and none of them answer a buyer who simply wants a later start date. The one mechanism that would have (a deposit to hold the deal and the price) exists in the team's practice but is not in the playbook and was not offered.

unmet_demand.want: A $5,000 price for the six-month programme, escalated to Trevor
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not a listed tier. The request was made explicitly and received no answer of any kind — not accepted, not declined, not promised onward. Whether it would be entertained is genuinely unresolved and needs a human decision before the 24 July call.
